review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. North Pacific ocean-migration studies support a 15 °C SST boundary and 4-16 °C surface-water exposure; bathymetry is not steelhead vertical depth.

profile.size: Min limit Varies by river/zone / Bag limit 1-2 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for steelhead.
factors.value_notes: A 1989 North Pacific ocean-migration synthesis found the southern limit of steelhead migration closely associated with the 15 °C sea-surface isotherm. A 2022 pop-up satellite tagging study of 63 Alaska steelhead kelts recorded a 4-16 °C thermal environment from June-January; fish spent most time in surface waters under 5 m. This supports marine SST relevance and overlaps the configured 8-16 °C / 10-14 °C bands, but is not a stock-specific catch-probability curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for steelhead.
factors.value_notes: Steelhead are epipelagic during ocean migration, principally within 10 m of the surface; 2022 satellite tags recorded most time in the upper 5 m and occasional dives to 15-20 m. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not fish vertical depth. The configured 0-40 m seabed range is only a weak coastal/shelf context proxy.
